info.title: Youjaymharah custom API
info.description:
Endpoints added by this project, on top of the Medusa Store and Admin APIs.

Medusa's own routes (products, carts, orders, customers, returns, ...) are
documented separately and can be downloaded from:

- Store: https://docs.medusajs.com/api/download/store
- Admin: https://docs.medusajs.com/api/download/admin

Every /store route also requires the `x-publishable-api-key` header.
Admin routes marked with `x-required-policies` need those RBAC policies,
which the Store Manager and Marketing roles already hold.

backendUrl.description: Base URL of the Medusa backend.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Full-text product search over the Search Module's index, with counted facets for refining a results page.

tags.name: Storefront
tags.description: Settings the storefront renders with, edited from Settings › Storefront: home page content (hero, featured collection), sharing & search defaults (title, description, share image, social profiles, indexing, Search Console verification) and product display (New badge days). The public route also includes the brand.

tags.name: Size guides
tags.description: Measurement tables for product pages. A product shows its own guide, else the nearest category's (walking up the category tree), else the store default. Measurements are stored in cm; the storefront converts to inches for display.

tags.name: Product alerts
tags.description: "Notify me" for sold-out sizes and coming-soon products. One email per alert, sent within about 10 minutes of the item becoming buyable, then the alert is done. Asking for an alert is not marketing consent.

tags.name: Marketing
tags.description: A signed-in customer's marketing email preference, backed by the newsletter list and its double opt-in.

tags.name: Branding
tags.description: The store's name, logo and support email, used across customer emails and the storefront.

tags.name: Newsletter
tags.description: Signup, double opt-in confirmation and unsubscribe, plus the admin side: settings, subscribers and the Resend audiences they sync to.

tags.name: Cart reminders
tags.description: Emails reminding shoppers about carts they left (their "shopping bag" on the storefront), at up to three delays after the cart's last change, with links to restore the cart or stop reminders.

tags.name: Accounts
tags.description: Customer accounts beyond Medusa's built-in routes: finishing a social sign-in so one person keeps one customer record.

tags.name: Wishlist
tags.description: Products a shopper has saved. One entry per product, optionally remembering the colour and size they chose. Signed-in customers use /store/customers/me/wishlist; guests use /store/wishlists, where the wishlist ID works like a guest cart's ID, and the guest list is merged into the customer's at sign-in.

get.summary: Get the size guide for a product page
get.description: The product's own guide, else the nearest category's, else the store default. `size_guide` is null when none applies: hide the size guide link. Measurements are in cm; convert for an inches view. Reads no customer data, so it is safe for cached pages.

get.description: Counts only, per variant; a null `variant_id` counts alerts for any size.

401.description: Missing or invalid admin token or session.

post.summary: Turn coming soon on or off
post.description: Sets `metadata.coming_soon` without touching other metadata. While on, the product stays published, can't be added to a cart or checked out, and shoppers can ask to be notified. Turning it off emails waiting shoppers on the next alert run once the product has stock. Turning it off on a product that was coming soon is its launch: `metadata.launched_at` is set to now (ISO 8601), which the storefront's "New" badge counts from.

200.description: The new setting, and the launch date if the product has ever been launched from coming soon.

401.description: Missing or invalid admin token or session.

post.summary: Ask to be notified when a product can be bought
post.description: For a sold-out variant (or product) or a coming-soon product. Signed in, the account's email is used and any `email` in the body is ignored; as a guest, `email` is required. Nothing is emailed until the item can be bought. Asking again for the same item returns the waiting alert. `marketing_opt_in` also signs the address up for the newsletter, with its confirmation email; a closed newsletter does not fail the request. Guests always get `alert: null`, so the response does not reveal existing alerts.

400.description: Validation failed, no email for a guest, the variant is not part of the product, the item can be bought now, or the address is waiting on 50 items already.

get.description: Waiting and sent alerts, newest first, up to 100. IDs only: load products through /store/products.

post.description: Call this with the token from GET /auth/customer/{provider}/callback instead of POST /store/customers. If the provider-verified email already has an account, the sign-in method is attached to it and that customer is returned (`linked: true`); otherwise a new customer is created. Only providers that verify email ownership (currently Google) may link; an emailpass identity is rejected.

200.description: The customer this sign-in now belongs to.

400.description: The sign-in returned no email address.

401.description: No auth token was provided.

403.description: This sign-in method may not be linked to an existing account.

post.summary: Set a password on an account that has none
post.description: For customers who signed up with Google and want to sign in with a password too. The email is taken from the logged-in account, not the request. Refused when the account already has a password — that is a reset, not a set.

400.description: The password is shorter than 8 characters.

401.description: No customer is logged in.

403.description: This account already has a password; use the reset flow instead.

get.description: Full-text search over published products in the sales channels the publishable key allows, with counted facets for refining the results. Returns the index' own fields rather than product rows: prices depend on region, currency and any active price list, so fetch /store/products with the returned ids to show them. Repeat a filter parameter to pass several values; values within one filter are OR-ed, and separate filters are AND-ed.

post.summary: Receive signed Resend consent and suppression events
post.description: Requires svix-id, svix-timestamp, and svix-signature computed over the original request bytes. No publishable key or customer session is used. Supports contact.updated opt-outs, permanent email.bounced, email.complained, email.suppressed and suppression.added. Other events are acknowledged without changing consent. Delivery limit: 64 KiB.

200.description: Acknowledged after workflow handling; duplicates are safe.

400.description: Invalid signature, delivery timestamp or event body.

500.description: Processing failed. Retry the delivery; pending receipts are also recovered by a scheduled job.
